reason: No defensible nitrate-groundwater concentration in mg/L NO3-N representing all incorporated and unincorporated Monterey County from the last five years was established in the inspected sources. Recent individual-well and subbasin measurements exist; averaging them without a representative sampling frame, coverage and weighting would create an unsupported county value. This finding does not assert that no suitable dataset exists.
nearest_data: Current local-government monitoring was examined before state sources. Monterey Subbasin WY2025 report, section 4.4.3.2 (printed p.87 / PDF p.95), reports selected coastal-well nitrate results from non-detect to approximately 6 mg/L as N, including approximately 5 mg/L in MCWD-30; these are selected wells, not a county statistic (https://www.mcwd.org/docs/gsa/3-004.10_WY_2025.pdf). The Water Board 2025 agricultural memo Figure 2 has 2024 NO3-N distributions and sample counts by subbasin, including East Side, Forebay, Upper Valley and 180/400 Foot; these on-farm domestic wells do not cover all county groundwater (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/water_issues/programs/ilp/docs/2025/gw-quality-tech-memo.pdf). The 2024 GAP report Tables 2–3 reports 253 Monterey wells tested and 141 nitrate-MCL exceedances over October 2018–July 2024; this voluntary cumulative sample is neither a recent concentration nor representative county coverage (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/board_info/agendas/2024/dec/item12_stfrpt.pdf). The 2024 Aquifer Risk Map layer uses depth-filtered/de-clustered well data but exposes a 20-year comparison-concentration index, recent exceedance counts and risk classes, not a recent county concentration (https://gispublic.waterboards.ca.gov/portalserver/rest/services/Hosted/Water_Quality_Risk_2024_ARM/FeatureServer/5). County monitoring manual access failed with HTTP 403 in web and evidence capture (https://www.countyofmonterey.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/135929/638648527079730000).
